newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cyprus central bank approves Italian cement deal.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus central bank approves Italian cement deal.

text.p: Cyprus's central bank has approved Italy's Italcementi purchase of shares in Vassiliko cement, a Cypriot newspaper reported on Thursday.
The deal increases the Italian company's stake in Vassiliko to 33 percent of capital from the 20 percent it acquired in 1990.
"We were obliged to approve the application before us based on our policy for foreign investments," central bank governor Afxentis Afxentiou told Philelephtheros newspaper.

The purchase has been the subject of controversy locally. Local opposition to the deal has been spearheaded by businessman Stavros Galatariotis who made a bid to buy the same company but failed when the Italians stepped in. The issue was the subject of a heated parliamentary inquiry last week.

Galatariotis's Cyprus Cement Company has challenged the deal, saying that Cyprus's Greek Orthodox Archbishop Chrysostomos reneged on a "gentleman's agreement" to sell Cyprus Cement the bulk of Vassiliko shares.
Chrysostomos is one of the largest shareholders in Vassiliko, which is controlled by the Hellenic Company Group.

Cyprus cement says it agreed with the Archbishop to buy 39 percent of Vassiliko shares at 209 cents -- but that deal was scuppered at the last minute when Italcementi came along to offer 240 per share.
Earlier this week Galatariotis made another bid to buy Vassiliko shares, offering 245 per share.
Under central bank regulations foreign investors are allowed to hold up to 49 percent of capital in a local company, and 15 percent in banks.
